options.name: A — the control plus the registry sentence (what ships now)
options.claim: The incumbent of this item, and the row every delta below is read against: the control carries its registry id, and the element around it DECLARES itself the context, printing the sentence the registry owns for that destination ("The club keeps its own Discord server, and the invite adds you to it."). The block is 23 words beside the label, which is the whole of the fix — the reader learns what the button enrols them in before they press it. This shape is what `check:cta-context` reads off the artifact; it is not a layout the page happens to have.

options.name: B — the label alone (what shipped on 2026-11-20)
options.claim: Exactly the shape the operator pointed at: a secondary control under the heading, its id and its sentence removed, nothing around it claiming to be its context. The reading calls it `action-undeclared` before it says anything about words — there are no words to weigh. This was not one call site: the research over the artifact of that date counted 49 marked links on 6 built pages, found the proximity window failing 0 of them and the block measure failing 17 — `/chat`'s own invite among them at 0 words @measured 2026-11-20 by `node design/cta-inventory.mjs`, in docs/research/discord-invite-ux-2026-11-20.md §5. Which is why the fix is an idiom and not a patch to /chat.

options.name: C — the accessible name fixed, nothing painted
options.claim: The half-fix, and the row that says why an accessible name is not the same thing as context: the anchor still declares its id and still carries the sr-only qualifier (" on Discord, opens in a new tab"), so a screen reader reads "Join the chat on Discord, opens in a new tab" — and a sighted reader sees two words and an arrow. The reading refuses it as `block-missing`: there is no element around the control claiming to be its context, so nothing painted names the server the invite enrols you in. `check:ext-links` is green on this row (0 findings, printed in the table beside it), which is the point — a green outbound-link gate coexisted with the defect the operator reported.

options.name: D — the control inside the page's own prose
options.claim: The same destination in the other shape the idiom allows: here the PAGE owns the block — a `<section>` whose own lead sentence is "The people, on an ordinary day, in the club’s own Discord server." No gloss is printed by the component, because the prose is already there and a component that appended a sentence every time would write boilerplate over the page's own words. It carries more than three times the floor (20 words beside the label against a floor of 6), and the extra words are the club's, not the registry's. This is the shape to choose where the page already has something to say; A is the shape for where it does not — and the same id, the same registry row and the same reading accept both, which is what stops a sweep of 43 actions from becoming 43 copies of one sentence.

options.name: E — one block, three actions: the exit band
options.claim: The multi-id shape: one element declaring three ids, so the band's two standing sentences are read as the context for the calendar feed, the Meetup group and the Discord invite at once — and each of the three is weighed against its own row (the feed must name a feed and an ask; the invite must name a server). The price of the shape is visible in the numbers: one block has to carry enough words for the most demanding of its three rows, and it must not swallow the page (over two thirds of the page's words fails as `block-too-wide`, which is what stops a `<main>`-sized wrap from laundering every action on it).
options.ruled: S090 (the multi-id form), D307 (the band is standing chrome)

options.name: F — the exit demoted to a quiet underlined label
options.claim: The operator's second question — "it feels incorrect for us to use a button there for something that takes you off the page. Shouldn't it be an anchor link" — answered as a weight question, not a meaning question. The site already ships a third step below primary and secondary: the quiet underlined label, byte-for-byte the classes the `/dates` rows use for a per-date sign-up (read out of the built page, not retyped here). This row pays the context rule the same way A does — the block and the id are untouched — and its cost is elsewhere: the anchor stops carrying `data-control`, so it leaves the control census that `check:render` measures and `check:primary-action` counts. What this round does NOT price is the fold: D367 holds the invite in the first screen, and whether a quiet label still sits there is a pixel question for `check:render` and `design/fold-answers.mjs`, not a number this row can honestly print.
options.ruled: open — the operator's question, priced for meaning only

options.name: G — the glyph removed from an exit that keeps its qualifier
options.claim: The operator's third question — "Shouldn't it be an anchor link with an external icon?" — as a measurement rather than an opinion. `check:ext-links` (S041, D317) demands `rel`, `target`, the sr-only qualifier and one name per platform; it does NOT demand the glyph, and this row proves it: with the arrow deleted the page is still green under that gate and still `ok` under the context rule. So the arrow is a design choice, and the choice this tree made is documented rather than implied — an `aria-hidden` glyph after an off-site control, and never after a same-site route (`ctaPlatform` is the only authority on "off-site", and D264 is why `check:cta-context` is written to fail a control that fakes the mark).
options.ruled: the arrow is not gated — this row is the evidence

notes: Every row is a byte delta on the built page in dist/client, applied to a copy under .design/tmp-round20/ and re-read by design/cta-rules.mjs — the same reading scripts/check-cta-context.mjs enforces, so a specimen number and a gate finding cannot come from different memories of the page (D264).

No pixel is measured in this round. Nothing here claims a height, a box, or a position relative to a fold; check:render and design/fold-answers.mjs price painted geometry when a variant graduates, and a specimen that printed a geometry number it never measured would be the defect D269 exists to stop.

The context rule at the time of this run: a block must hold at least 6 words besides the action's own label, and may account for at most 67% of its page's words (src/lib/links.mjs, CTA_BLOCK_MIN_WORDS / CTA_BLOCK_MAX_FRACTION).
